question.text: Vindhya Turnaround Fund is a Cat II AIF constituted as a trust. In FY25 it books INR 12 crore of income that the tax auditor concludes is 'business income'. How is this INR 12 crore taxed?

answer.text: Passed through to unit-holders in their slab/rate
Taxed at the fund level at MMR under Section 10(23FBB) (trust); exempt in investors' hands
Exempt entirely because all AIF income is pass-through

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 115UB read with Section 10(23FBB) carves out business income from pass-through. Because the fund is a trust (not a company/firm), business income is taxed AT THE FUND at MMR. The trade-off: it is then EXEMPT in the unit-holder's hands. If the AIF had been an LLP/company, business income would be taxed at the LLP/company slab. The Trap: Option A is the Cat I/II rule for NON-business income. Option C is the LTCG rate. Option D wrongly generalises pass-through to all heads. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A tests 'pass-through' as a slogan; XIX-C requires knowing the carve-out and its structural driver (trust vs LLP). Manager's Pro-Tip: Avoid commingling frequent-trading strategies into a Cat II distressed/turnaround fund — the business-income taint at MMR can wipe out 42.7% of the P&L versus 12.5% LTCG on capital-asset exits. Post Finance Act 2025, Section 2(14) helps Cat I/II because all securities are capital assets — use this in PPM.
